source.authors: Peichl L, Radic T, Solovei I, Wolfram M, Glösmann M
source.title: On the retinae of Glis and Graphiurus: photoreceptor and ganglion cell populations, an absence of shortwave-sensitive cones, and some other features (Rodentia: Gliridae)

method: anatomical: estimate from peak retinal ganglion cell density (NeuN-labelled presumed RGCs, about 4000 per mm2 in temporal central retina)
where: Abstract; two consecutive pieces returned by the fetch tool, split after 'cycles/degree'
quote: The peak ganglion cell density would result in an estimated visual acuity maximum of ca. 1.8 cycles/degree or ca. 33 minutes of arc.
note: Value as given by the source (ca. 1.8 cycles/degree, equal to ca. 33 minutes of arc). Fat dormouse; nearest measured relative of Muscardinus (different genus, so not carried).

source.authors: Peichl L, Radic T, Solovei I, Wolfram M, Glösmann M
source.title: On the retinae of Glis and Graphiurus: photoreceptor and ganglion cell populations, an absence of shortwave-sensitive cones, and some other features (Rodentia: Gliridae)

method: opsin immunolabelling of the retina (L cones only) and SWS1 opsin gene sequencing
where: Abstract; two consecutive pieces returned by the fetch tool, split after 'in most mammals,'
quote: There are no S cones expressing the shortwave-sensitive (SWS1) opsin that is the second cone opsin in most mammals, conveying dichromatic colour vision. We conclude that the fat dormouse is a cone monochromat.
note: One cone class (LWS) plus rods; the SWS1 gene is non-functional. Value 1 is the number of cone classes, taken from the source's wording 'cone monochromat'. Nearest measured relative of Muscardinus (different genus).
